rationale: This is algebraically almost the same object as the archive's cash_coverage_of_required_investment (oancf/max(capx+aqc, dp), alpha 0.041, t 3.36) — surplus cash deflated by depreciation is a reparametrization of that same coverage ratio using identical inputs — so it is a cosmetic re-scaling rather than a new mechanism, and free-cash-flow-to-capital-consumption is itself close to published FCF/investment-anomaly territory.

The construct is coherent and sign-consistent, but it is essentially spanned by three existing archive signals (cash_generation_vs_acquisitive_expansion, cash_generation_vs_serial_acquisitiveness, unearned_goodwill_without_cash_flow_growth) and amounts to swapping one already-tested leg for another already-tested leg, i.e. a component recombination rather than a new economic channel.

Economically sensible and internally consistent, but it differs from cash_flow_payoff_on_cumulative_investment only by adding aqc to the denominator — a single-term tweak with identical data requirements, so the claim that it will lift coverage above 0.064 is unfounded and the proposal reads as a robustness variant rather than a substantively different design.

Extending the funding-gap numerator to a three-year cumulative deficit while holding the liquidity buffer contemporaneous is a legitimate persistence test (chronic external dependence vs a transitory capex spike) with a correctly signed expression, though the mixed flow/stock deflator MAX(che, TS_SUM(dp,3)) makes the units of the ratio firm-dependent and should be diagnosed if results diverge from the one-year version.

The hypothesis says the cash cow must be "not merely high but steady," yet the expression contains no cash-flow *level* at all — a firm with negligible but placid cash flow scores maximally — and the low-volatility leg largely rediscovers the known earnings/cash-flow-volatility and low-risk anomalies rather than adding a cross-theme interaction.

The "mix" is not actually measured: firms with zero R&D score identically whether they are serial acquirers or pure non-investors, so for the bulk of the cross-section the second leg collapses to R&D/depreciation — i.e. the well-documented R&D-intensity anomaly stacked on a cash-profitability rank — rather than a build-versus-buy contrast.
